title: Contrast and Accessibility
slide_intent: Compare marks against their actual backgrounds so numerical contrast and visual comfort both inform the choice.
strategic_value: Consistent background decisions can make T-Mobile marks easier to identify in partner environments.
demonstration: Approved brand colorways sit above blue, red and gray background tests labeled with pass/fail results.
practical_value: Use the examples to identify risky combinations, then check the actual artwork with a contrast tool.

content_islands.name: Contrast rationale
content_islands.spec: Place explanatory copy and the color-burning caution in the left column.

content_islands.name: Brand combinations
content_islands.spec: Align five marked examples across the upper-right row.

content_islands.name: External background tests
content_islands.spec: Group three logo colors over each of three non-brand backgrounds below.

ingredient.name: Mark/background contrast
ingredient.role: Keep the brand symbol easy to distinguish from its field.
ingredient.application: Choose a clear approved colorway and test actual contrast. Inspect magenta combinations for visual vibration even when a contrast test passes. Obtain Brand team approval for non-T-Mobile executions.
ingredient.scope: All brand marks covered by the February 2024 guide, in print and digital applications. The page labels its examples against WCAG 2.0 AA; these labels are source claims, not a new accessibility audit.

reference_purposes.Intent: The text connects mark/background contrast to viewability and explains why magenta combinations also need inspection for visual vibration.
reference_purposes.Application: Five brand colorways and three groups of external-background tests demonstrate how to compare mark and field; the text calls for contrast-checking tools.
reference_purposes.Constraint: The page marks specific combinations as failing its stated criteria and requires Brand team approval for non-T-Mobile executions.
